latestRelease.name: pandoc 3.13
latestRelease.releaseNotes:
I'm pleased to announce the release of pandoc 3.13,
available in the usual places:

Binary packages & changelog:
https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/tag/3.13

Source & API documentation:
http://hackage.haskell.org/package/pandoc-3.13

This release fixes some regressions and makes many minor
improvements.  See the changelog for full details.

Behavior changes:

- Locations of errors in default files are now reported.
- YAML is now parsed with the yamlet library, which implements
  YAML 1.2. As a result, we'll get better error messages, and:

  + `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `y` and `n` are strings, not booleans.
  + Duplicate keys in a mapping are an error. They were a warning.
  + `.5`, `.inf` and `.nan` are numbers.

  The most likely way this change will bite you is if you use
  `no` in a boolean field. This will be interpreted as a nonempty
  value, which will be treated as truthy in a template.

API changes:

- Text.Pandoc.Sharde: export `plainToPara` and `paraToPlain`.
- Text.Pandoc.Writers.Shared: export new functions `wrapColumns` and
  `rendereWithTemplate`.
- Text.Pandoc.Translations: `readTranslations` now takes the path
  of the file as ar

latestRelease.name: v17.13.0
latestRelease.releaseNotes:
**Changes**

- PDF/A made without Ghostscript ("speculative" conversion) is now validated
  with pikepdf's PDF/A support (`pikepdf.pdfa`) instead of veraPDF, and the
  final output is validated again after the metadata and optimization steps.
  veraPDF is no longer used, so the Ghostscript-free path is available
  whether or not veraPDF is installed, including in the Docker image. Files
  the validator does not approve go to Ghostscript as before; run with `-v1`
  to see why.
- Speculative conversion now supports PDF/A-1b, and repairs common problems
  that previously always sent a file to Ghostscript: it replaces other output
  intents with sRGB, removes image interpolation flags, sets the Print flag on
  annotations, adds the `/CIDSet` PDF/A-1 requires, and removes XMP properties
  and hidden annotations that PDF/A does not permit.
- New option `--pdfa-backend {auto,ghostscript,internal}` (API:
  `pdfa_backend=`). `auto`, the default, tries OCRmyPDF's own conversion and
  then Ghostscript. `internal` never uses Ghostscript, so JPEGs pass through
  unchanged; if the result is not approved, the `pdfa` output types fail with
  exit code 10 and `--output-type auto` outputs a regular

**Security**

- The published `ia` pex binary for 5.12.0 bundled certifi 2026.7.22, which
  still trusts the emSign root CAs whose intermediate keys were compromised
  (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2). This release rebuilds the binary with certifi
  2026.10.19. `certifi>=2026.10.19` is now also a declared dependency, so
  `pip install -U internetarchive` carries the fix into existing environments.
- Development and CI dependencies updated past their open advisories:
  urllib3 2.8.0 (CVE-2026-97687, CVE-2026-97688, CVE-2026-97689) and
  virtualenv 21.14.12 (sixteen activation-script and seed-wheel advisories).
- `ia --insecure` now prints a warning to stderr on every invocation that the
  request, including S3 keys and cookies, goes over unencrypted HTTP, and its
  `--help` text says the same. A `SECURITY.md` documents how to report
  vulnerabilities privately.
- The `ia` pex binary is now built from the versions pinned in `uv.lock`,

  on build day. The build fails if any dependency lacks a universal wheel, so

latestRelease.name: qpdf version 12.4.2
latestRelease.releaseNotes:
This is qpdf version 12.4.2. In addition to a few small bug fixes, this release features two significant improvements: inclusion of several new binary platform releases and substantial improvements to linearization. We now include official release binaries for MacOS (intel and arm64), Windows arm64, and Linux aarch64 (arm64) both as an AppImage and as stand-alone binaries. For linearization, for certain types of files, qpdf is vastly more memory efficient (we've seen 30× improvements in some cases) and slightly faster. Also, there are a few small fixes to linearization object ordering, so linearized output may differ for some rare files relative to previous releases.

For a full list of changes from previous releases, please see the [release notes](https://qpdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/release-notes.html). See also [README-what-to-download](./README-what-to-download.md) for details about the available source and binary distributions.

This release was signed by ejb@ql.org.
